headline: MP MATERIALS SUES USA RARE EARTH OVER STOLEN MAGNET TRADE SECRETS — GRAIN BOUNDARY DIFFUSION TECH AT STAKE
snippet: MP Materials (NYSE: MP) filed a Texas lawsuit alleging a former engineer stole proprietary "grain boundary diffusion" formulations for rare earth permanent magnets and passed them to USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR), which then disclosed the technology to a third-party manufacturer. The case escalates the U.S. domestic rare earth supply chain race into a full IP war — with $354 million in Pentagon magnet contracts hanging in the balance.

headline: ZIJIN'S $4B ALLIED GOLD DEAL IN JEOPARDY — CHINA'S NDRC QUESTIONS MALI RISK, DEAL MAY COLLAPSE
snippet: Hours after Allied Gold cleared the Investment Canada Act hurdle, the Financial Times reported China's NDRC is reconsidering whether to approve the deal at all — questioning whether the slim ~5% premium is justified given the political and operational risks of Allied's Mali assets, which generate roughly half of its gold output. Allied Gold (TSX: AAUC) shares fell 5.6% on the news; the outside date is now July 29.

headline: BAYHORSE SILVER COMMENCES 2,000-METRE UNDERGROUND DRILL CAMPAIGN — TARGETS 1,104 g/t SILVER ZONE IN BRITISH COLUMBIA
snippet: Bayhorse Silver (TSX-V: BHS) commenced its 13-hole, 2,000-metre underground diamond drill program at its British Columbia silver mine June 1, targeting the high-priority CR-2 IP anomaly to the south and easterly extensions. A prior groundwater test well at the property intercepted 1.5 metres grading 1,104 g/t silver — one of the highest-grade intercepts from any British Columbia silver project in recent years.

headline: ENERGY STORAGE BOOM DRIVES 55% LITHIUM DEMAND SURGE IN 2026 — MARKET DEFICIT SIGNALS EMERGE BY H2
snippet: Lithium demand for grid-scale battery energy storage is forecast to jump 55% in 2026, following a 71% surge in 2025, lifting energy storage's share of total lithium consumption to 31% from 23% last year. China's aggressive BESS buildout is absorbing supply faster than the market expected, with analysts now projecting the market tips from chronic oversupply into deficit by H2 2026 — a potential turning point for beaten-down lithium equities.

headline: CHINA'S ACID BAN CRUSHES COPPER SMELTERS WORLDWIDE — $6.40/LB RECORD SET AS 3 MILLION TONNES OF CAPACITY GOES DARK
snippet: China's May-to-December ban on sulfuric acid exports has removed an estimated 3 million tonnes of global copper smelting capacity from the seaborne market, compounding Chile's already weak supply chain and helping push copper to a record $6.40/lb. The supply shock has flipped the ICSG's 2026 balance from a 209,000-tonne surplus to a deficit — a structurally bullish signal for copper development-stage junior miners.

headline: AI DATA CENTRE BUILDOUT SET TO TURBOCHARGE URANIUM DEMAND — NUCLEAR NOW CENTRAL TO BIG TECH ENERGY STRATEGY
snippet: Artificial intelligence data centres are emerging as the most powerful new structural driver of global electricity demand, with major technology firms signing long-term nuclear power purchase agreements and lobbying for accelerated reactor licensing. The trend reinforces the uranium investment thesis beyond the existing grid decarbonisation narrative and tightens the supply-demand balance heading into H2 2026.

headline: GOLD, SILVER AND COPPER: WHY THE METALS DESK IS STILL BULLISH DESPITE THE MAY CORRECTION
snippet: A GoldSeek market update argues the May correction in precious and base metals is a positioning event rather than a trend change — pointing to persistent central bank gold buying, the structural silver deficit entering its sixth year, and the copper supply gap to make the case that the commodity bull market is intact heading into H2 2026.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER CORRECTION IN JUNE: KEY SUPPORT LEVELS AND THE YIELD CURVE SIGNAL TO WATCH
snippet: Technical and macro analysis of the current precious metals correction identifies critical support zones for gold and silver entering June 2026. The piece focuses on the unusual yield-curve dynamic driving gold lower despite active Middle East conflict — and examines where the next inflection point may emerge for patient long-term buyers in the junior mining sector.

headline: JUNIOR GOLD MINERS REGAIN MOMENTUM AS PRODUCER MARGINS HIT RECORD — NAV DISCOUNTS WIDEN TO HISTORIC LOWS
snippet: VanEck's Imaru Casanova argues that gold mining equities — particularly junior developers — are generating record operating margins near $2,800/oz while trading at 0.6–0.8× NAV, valuations more typical of a bear market than a $4,400 gold environment. As producers demonstrate capital discipline and accelerate buybacks, the setup favours equity re-rating over physical metal for investors with a 12–18 month horizon.

headline: DISCOVERY SILVER POSTS SOLID Q1 2026 EARNINGS AND CASH FLOW — CORDERO DEVELOPMENT TIMELINE ON TRACK
snippet: Discovery Silver Corp (TSX: DSV) reported solid Q1 2026 earnings and cash flow, keeping its flagship Cordero silver-gold-zinc-lead project in Mexico on schedule for development. Cordero is one of the largest undeveloped primary silver projects in the world — its progress is a bellwether for the broader junior silver development sector.
